content: CSS custom properties in SVG <style> blocks provide the cleanest design token approach for hand-authored SVGs at scale. Defining semantic tokens (--color-primary, --stroke-muted, etc.) in a shared spec document and copying a consistent <style> block header into each SVG gives visual consistency without tooling. The key constraint: for inline SVGs, a per-file <style> block that references shared class names (.ttl, .sub, .lab, .sm, .mono) is more maintainable than CSS custom properties because the inline SVGs render in page context where page CSS can interfere. The fdars de-facto baseline already uses this class-name pattern consistently across ~35 diagrams; the remaining ~8-9 diagrams use older font-family attributes and non-standard viewBox sizes and need to be brought into alignment.
